f2_architecture_context.finding: F2 already distinguishes dashboard intent from host-produced permission evidence, but the source explicitly delegates actual OS/native checks to a not-yet-proven host adapter. HostPermissionGrant.native_permission_ref is structurally only a non-empty string and the effective-host-permission marker is derived at resolution time; no portal session liveness/revocation witness is represented by this module alone.

upstream_pins.official_docs_surface: PipeWire 1.6.8 Portal Access Control / Access Control
upstream_pins.scope_note: Documentation establishes portal-managed restricted PipeWire connections and dynamic per-object permission revocation; the documentation deployment is not claimed byte-identical to the observed GitHub mirror commit.

source_findings.finding: ScreenCast uses an explicit long-lived portal Session. A session can be closed by the client or portal at any time; Session.Closed signals closure, and disappearance of the D-Bus client is equivalent to closing its active sessions.
source_findings.f2_implication_hypothesis: A static grant marker cannot by itself prove continued authorization after session closure.

source_findings.finding: ScreenCast restore tokens are single-use persistence/restore tokens. Withdrawal of stored permission can make restoration fail and prompt again. persist_mode describes persistence, not proof that an already compiled ObserveIntent remains currently executable.
source_findings.f2_implication_hypothesis: Never use restore_token as a current-permission/liveness credential.

source_findings.finding: ScreenCast interface version 6 deprecates the returned PipeWire node ID for targeting because node IDs can be reused after node destruction. It directs consumers to pipewire-serial/object.serial plus PW_KEY_TARGET_OBJECT. Stream id is opaque/session-local and may persist across restored sessions.
source_findings.f2_implication_hypothesis: F2 capture identity should not authorize or causally bind a stream by reusable node ID alone.

source_findings.finding: OpenPipeWireRemote yields a file descriptor for a portal-configured PipeWire remote. ScreenCast exposes only the selected screencast nodes; Camera OpenPipeWireRemote succeeds only after camera permission and exposes camera nodes.
source_findings.f2_implication_hypothesis: The live remote/session is an execution capability and should remain ephemeral; durable state should store typed digests/receipts, not a raw file descriptor.

source_findings.finding: PipeWire portal access starts from a restricted connection; the session manager grants visibility/interaction on permitted objects and can remove permissions when permission state changes. PipeWire permissions are per client/object and can change during a client lifetime.
source_findings.f2_implication_hypothesis: Execution-time permission revalidation or a revocation-aware lease is required if F2 wants current host-authorization evidence rather than only compile-time evidence.

source_findings.finding: ScreenCast is explicitly session-oriented with source selection and Start/OpenPipeWireRemote. Camera uses AccessCamera then OpenPipeWireRemote and is not described by the same ScreenCast session protocol.
source_findings.f2_implication_hypothesis: Do not force one fake universal portal-session shape across all PerceptionSource kinds; use a common typed host-permission ABI with source-specific native evidence adapters.

hypothesis: For Linux visual capture, F2 should structurally distill portal/PipeWire semantics into a thin source-specific host adapter that binds user policy to fresh native permission/session evidence, stable stream identity and revocation-aware execution validation, while retaining UnifiedDB/F2 as the only canonical state authority.
counterhypothesis: The existing monotonic HostPermissionGrant expiry plus effective marker could be sufficient if every actual capture invocation unconditionally reacquires native permission and never relies on a previously compiled ObserveIntent. Current inspected F2 source does not yet establish that execution-time reacquisition invariant.
recommended_next_discriminator: E2 map the exact minimal adapter/lease boundary against current F2 perception source and prove whether compile-time effective permission can remain valid after an external session closes. Do not import portal or PipeWire frameworks merely to copy their policy layer.
